Let's start with the positive aspects:
- There are three different campaigns  plus a forth one featuring the all-mysterious Ada Wong which was originally a DLC

So far, RE6 looks like a decent sequel to RE5 (which was an excellent game IMHO). 

Here's the part that can break an RE fan's heart:
In essence, RE6 miserably fails to deliver a good gameplay.

1) I have always liked the RE cut scenes and I think they are a vital part of the game. But interrupting the gameplay every two minutes simply ruins the atmosphere. I cannot even begin to fathom why the devs chose to script virtually everything in the game. And it's not just the cut scenes: In almost every level you will find that your protagonist struggles to keep on his feet: Ground shaking, ceiling collapsing, plane crashing, diving, sliding, etc. While that may be realistic, it really bugs me if the surroundings constantly throw off my aim when I am trying to survive through a nightmare of collapsing scenery. 

2) You will be set under pressure. A LOT of times. Generally, enforcing time limits on the player in certain scenarios can help to invoke a dramatic flair and it will get your heart pumping. However, if you constantly put the player into hour-long scenarios where you have to run / escape because virtually everything around you collapses / explodes / gets flooded is a sure way of ruining any meaningful gaming experience. Exerting some pressure is okay, but please - for god's sake - let me look around the world. Take in some of the details. Let me do some strategic planning and not wildly running off from one cinematic to the next.

3) You will be forced along a very narrow road. In many of the action sequences when there is a time limit, you will be forced to follow a fixed path which is often not clear to you. Instead, you will often barely notice that the camera perspective is shifting, and that you have to run somewhere before you notice that you actually took too long and - of course - die instantly.
The problem is not that it is actually difficult to survive the countless Quick Time Events, no. It is that you often do not know what you need to do before it is too late. 

4) For some reason the devs thought that it would be a great idea to erratically and unpredictably fix the camera in a completely different perspective from time to time. Of course, that means that your character will automatically change direction if you keep your buttons / keys pressed while the camera changes. This is simply ridiculously bad.

5) Countless times, you will find yourself in a situation where you are fighting an infinite number of enemies, forcing you to quicken the pace and find a solution to one of the game's (mostly) lame puzzles or to quickly leave the current part of the level. This is both mindless and boring at the same time while adding virtually nothing to the gaming experience.

6) Where are the Zombies? Though you will face some of RE's most-famed enemies during the first campaign, you will suddenly find yourself fighting "mutated people / soldiers / mercenaries carrying firearms" almost all the time. This is one of the most criticized facts about the game that partly it feels more like a generic shooter like COD than like any RE part prior to it. The fact that you can also (slowly) move while aiming / firing your weapon and even dodge to the side / to the back does not really help matters. In fact, in earlier RE games I rather enjoyed having to weigh the consequences of fighting off an opponent with my weapon (but having to stop running) or running away to get in a better position to fight him.

7) One of the strongest aspects of the RE series are the bosses and the boss fights. While RE6 certainly comes up with some of the meanest, biggest and most impressive monstrosities of the series, the actual boss fights are either:
a) totally lame (because you have to wait for a stupid NPC  to finish something)
b) totally scripted
c) totally counter-intuitive (because you have not the faintest idea on how to hurt the boss)
d) totally ridiculous (because the boss is invincible)

8) Skill System. The game offers you to select up to three different skills, improving your damage, aim or abilities.  Skills can be unlocked and upgraded using skill points found during the game. While this sounds interesting at first, it gets boring quickly: You will soon notice that many of the skills are simply too ineffective or too specific to be useful on more than one occasion. 

9)  The menu system is needlessly cumbersome.

10) To find all the hidden serpent symbols which unlock the collectibles of the game is quite difficult. That was the same in e.g. RE5 and is not a bad thing in itself. What I truyl disliked is that at least one symbol is hidden in an action sequence where it is pure luck whether you initially pick it up or not. Missed it and wanna go back? Forget it. You have to restart the whole level again. Frustrated? Angry? Be my guest! 

11) While trying to tie the four campaigns together in the story, the devs have decided to have many overlaps in the level structure of the game. While this helps to certainly invoke a feeling of familiarity, it gets boring too quickly: Fighting the virtually same boss twice (just controlling a different character) is lame. Ironically, this will happen numerous times.

What really frustrates me the most is this: RE6 does have a huge potential. 
The first campaign of Leon and Helena is really good (leaving out the final levels, of course). 
Why Capcom has chosen to abandon the mood and atmosphere altogether in the subsequent campaigns will remain their secret. 

RE is about having a great atmosphere. There's almost nothing left of that in the game.

Once you have finished the whole game and watched the credit roll (EDIT: can only be skipped with 'backspace', thanks @ChenZhe.), you will realize that many dozens of people were involved in making this game. 
Didn't they ever realize that RE6 falls back behind its predecessor RE5 in purely every aspect of the game play? 
Didn't they ever realize that the replay value once you have soaked in all the cinematics is minimal?
Didn't they ever realize that constant pressure on the player and endless quick time events cannot compensate for a lack of atmosphere?
We will never know. 
I can recommend RE5 without hesitation to you and had RE6 been at least half as good, I would have recommended it, too. 

If you are a die-hard RE fan, you might want to get this game anyway, but honestly you can also look up the story in a let's play and you will not miss much.
I can only pray that Capcom will turn back to make RE7 more like the earlier titles of the series...

Resident Evil 6 is often called the worst of the main series, and that is probably true. Although, I personally believe this game gets more hate than it deserves.

Resident Evil 6 places you in the usual apocalyptic situation our protagonists somehow find themselves in. Unlike previous games, you have four separate stories to play through, all of which are intertwined in some way with each other.

I'll start with the negatives, as there are quite a few. First, the game's story is completely ridiculous at times. It has its good moments every now and then (especially at the end of Chris' campaign), but most of the time it feels confusing and really weird. It can get hard to follow as well. This is most likely because the game attempted to lean on action instead of horror while also trying to do horror, leaving it a muddled mess.

Second, the actual campaign flow for each campaign is horrendous. Large quiet sections often drag the game on while action sections come one after another, never really letting up (this is actually a positive which I will get into later). This is probably because they focused on making four separate campaigns instead of just one really good one, making each campaign feel half-baked in a sense (this is not the fault of the developers, more the fault of the people who actually set the deadlines).

Finally going back to the story, it doesn't really end on a single note. Thanks to it being split into multiple campaigns, the game relies on the final one to tie everything together. This results in the final campaign feeling really awkward and ending on a "okay, so what?" kind of note.

Okay so me saying all of this and still giving it a positive review must tell you that there's something else this game has going for it. And there is.

The gameplay.

Of any Resident Evil game, RE6 has the most engaging combat I've seen. From RE4 and RE5, the characters can still shoot enemies in their weakpoints and use melee attacks to deal extra damage. However there are so many more controls in RE6. You can dash and ram into enemies to stagger them. You can melee enemies to deliver a second blow with a powerful melee attack. You can slide into enemies to stagger them. You can dodge-roll to the side or backwards to evade attacks. You can even counter enemy attacks to deal heavy damage, often out-right killing the enemy. And there are far more controls than that that would take a long time to list out. There's a reason this game is said to have the best mercenaries mode. In fact, the game is best played foregoing your gun in favour of melee attacks against regular enemies (even on the highest difficulty and with infinite ammo).

This is why I believe the best way to play this game is not treat it as a Resident Evil game at all. Sure, as one it's terrible. But as a stand-alone game, it is a fantastic action game with a decent action-based story to go with it. There are still those really slow moments, sure, but when the game gets going, it gets going.

This is especially true on the highest difficulty, where the game pulls no punches. On Professional or No Hope, you are expected to display constant mastery of the game's controls or else you WILL be annihilated. It's an exhilarating experience to complete a chapter on one of the highest difficulties, especially with someone else helping out.

All in all, Resident Evil 6 fails hard as a Resident Evil game. It lacks the horror, resource management, and good story-telling that made the foundations of far better Resident Evil games like RE4 and RE7. However as its own thing, RE6 is a brilliant action game which shows you that when there's a zombie ahead and you have a gun, the best solution is to punch it in the face and break its spine. The game has a semi-decent story, and the difficulties allow both casual and experienced players to have a challenge to measure themselves up to.

[h1]Quick Summary[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 is an action/horror third person shooter game with co-op, puzzle, and story elements. It takes away the focus from horror and emphasizes the action and story compared to older RE games, while providing around 20 hours of campaign. 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
-Lots of content. There are 4 separate campaigns that can be played fully in co-op or alone, with cutscenes and multiple action sequences. 
-Intricate storyline with intertwining story arcs from the various characters. 
-Cutscenes and dialogue. They are all pretty good quality with good voice actors. 
-Overall fun gameplay with lots of different guns depending on the campaign and character you play.
-Each campaign is pretty varied from the other ones, with different melee animations, guns, locations, bosses, and even common enemies. This keeps each playthrough feeling fresh and new.

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-The primary con in my opinion is the forced “fixed camera angle” segments in the games. They often take place during boss battles or forced flight sequences, throwing in unnecessary awkwardness into gameplay. I do understand that this was a staple of the original titles, but as a newcomer to the series it felt very unfair and annoying to have to adjust everything I knew just for certain parts of the game, when the tension was already high enough. While playing co-op with my wife, we died so many times just during these parts where the camera was locked a certain way or made you run backwards for example, never during the actual combat. 
- You can’t skip the credits at the end of each campaign. 

[h1]Neutral[/h1]
-Less horror; more action. This depends on your preference. I thought the focus on action was pretty fun especially when you played as soldiers in Chris Redfield’s campaign. You’re able to kill zombies with powerful melee hits, many different firearms, grenades, and environmental tools. Not only that but you are able to dodge hits, roll, slide, and shoot while in cover or on the ground. This gives you many options for taking down enemies. However, this takes away some of the tension of previous games by eliminating the need for really conserving ammo or choosing your battles. 

[h1]Story Quality[/h1]
For the most part, Resident Evil 6 presents an interesting but somewhat predictable story. I did really enjoy how side characters in one campaign were playable in the next, so you got to see everything that happens in between. 

[h1]Technical Analysis[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 ran with no bugs or crashes in all 4 campaigns, so it runs great from a technical standpoint. I will say the user interface is different in each campaign and uses symbols instead of text, so it is not intuitive on which part of the menu is what you need. It uses a glaring, almost neon colored UI that I really did not enjoy. It also is quite different from previous games so it’s hard to get used to it, at least initially. Figuring out how to combine items or change ammo type in weapons was also not easy to figure out.
Resident Evil 6 is a bit older, so optimization was no issue. The textures were pretty blurry at times, but this is also a 6 year old game so I don’t feel I can complain too much. 

[h1]Price…is it worth it?[/h1]
I bought the game on sale at $7.49. At that price, I think it’s easily worth it and a no-brainer if you like Resident Evil games or even just want to shoot up some zombies for a few hours. It’s base price of $29.99 seems a bit high since it is older, so I would recommend if you are interested in this game, to buy it on sale. 

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Resident Evil 6 makes some bold moves in the franchise by taking away some of the tension, item management and horror of previous titles. However, as an action and story-driven game I believe it’s quite fun and especially enjoyable in co-op. I do recommend picking it up on sale though, as it’s a bit older and not a mind-blowing story.

After playing the second trilogy of Resident Evil, starting with RE4 and slowly building my way to the climax, Resident Evil 6 did not suprise me in how huge, ridiculous, goofy, tense, and fun it was. The fact that this game has gained as much hate as it has shows me that this series is personal to a lot of people, and everyone has a definition of what Resident Evil means to them. To those who define Resident Evil by the first trilogy (third person fixed cameras with survival horror camp), the hate is understandable. For those who played a majority of the first trilogy (I myself played/beat RE1 and 2, watched 3, and played Code: Veronica) and went on to embrace the larger plot which really did call for more of an action horror slant, Resident Evil 6 tied up everything with a huge bang as a lot of our favorite Resident Evil heroes save the world.

After playing a majority of the Resident Evil titles, I now know what Resident Evil means to me. As much as I love the original trilogy, I realize that RE means Chris, Jill, Leon, Claire, Barry, Rebecca, Ada Wong and numerous other RE heroes saving the world from Umbrella and various viruses in good old B survival or action horror camp, and enjoying the ride, no matter how ludicrous. If that rings a bell with you, read on.

(God bless you for reading on)

First lets deal with the technical. The game looks really great. The soundtrack is exciting and can be eerily quiet at times. The AI partners are not stupid (yes, Shiva from RE5, I'm looking at you!). I never had to worry about my partner running out of ammo unless I wanted to turn that option off, and I trusted that my partner would have my back. While the AI partner does help in a fight, it is you that has to deal the final blow to bosses. When I died, it was due to my lack of ability and not my partner doing their best to keep me alive. The combat was very smooth. I didn't always have to worry about lack of bullets, although they are scarce, because I could do martial arts. I loved being able to roundhouse enemies if I had too, and then stomp on them. Also, each character has a different fighting style. Some are fluid martial artists, while Chris is a soldier who isn't busy showing off his kung fu but throws a heavy punch showing off that famous bicep ;). 

The first technical negative I found was the different menu systems. They were a pain. Remember when you had one menu and you could do everything from that one menu? Well apparently thats too simple. In one menu, you can see all your stuff, but in another menu you combine herbs and reload your weapons. Trust me, when in the heat of battle, it is infuriating. Also, there really isn't a pause option. When you hit pause, your character will kneel down to look at their phone, hoping that whatever changes you need to make will be done quickly because the monsters are still attacking you. That was annoying. Also, remember in classic RE when you unlocked weapons and outfits, and they were yours? Well now its a little more complicated. Now you have to gain points by doing killing combos and then using said points to buy the weapons or outfits you unlocked. This may up the replayability but to me its just a slap in the face, adding more work when I technically feel that unlocking abilities and costumes should make them mine now!

The voice acting was superb. The script was very well done, with one liners that stood apart from the rest of the series (no Jill sandwich homage here). The relationships forged between partners was real. They had me tearing up at moments and then giving me sighs of contentment at others. Also, not every moment on this game was explosions and Sci-Fi Channel zombie ridiculousness. Sometimes the games was tight and quiet, and that to me was a nice nod to us old school RE fans that enjoyed slowly walking through corridors, wondering what C virus abomination we would face next. Or if we would run into the boss that just refused to die! The motto for the heroes of this game is never to get up. Well apparently the bosses overheard that pep talk and decided that was a good idea, because my goodness they just won't die! To me, the goofiest thing about the game is the sheer determination of this games bosses.

Now the campaigns. I loved them all for very different reasons. Leon's campaign by far is the most ridiculous and goofy. I bet its his campaign that gives the game its bad rap. Plus, there is no Claire. Leon is the one that is targeting the main antagonist of the game, and I enjoyed the exciting progression through the game. It was nice to see Ada Wong cross his path (though to be fair Ada Wong crosses everybody's path). Jake's campaign is awesome in that it pairs him with Sherry Birkin, a nod to all us RE2 fans. Now we get to see what happened to that sweet girl we protected all those years ago. While I have shipped other RE characters, this campaign definitely had a kind of underlying attraction between the two characters as they go from warily trusting each other, to sparks of gratitide and attraction. Its heartwarming amongst all the mutated zombies. Then Chris's campaign, which at first I didn't think I'd like because Chris is leading his soldiers on a different front then Leon or Jake, but that ties in perfectly with the story. It's much more than Chris and his squad shooting zombies. It is definitely more psychological, and telling why would be spoiling ;). After playing Leon's, Jake's, and Chris's campaign, the story will still not be complete. A few puzzles pieces are missing. Thats when you get to play Ada Wong's campaign and what a payoff. Ada knows what is up. She is behind the scenes tweaking the scenarios that in the other campaigns will make you think, "Well that was convenient! How did that happen?". Ada is happening everywhere, behind the scenes. The only puzzles you really will encounter are in her campaign, and they are nothing compared to the beginnings of the series, but then again they weren't a big thing in RE4 or RE5. By the end of Ada's campaign, you will know the whole story, and the trilogy is neatly tied up, and in my opinion Resident Evil is successfuly concluded.

Resident Evil is a mutation of a game series that has changed and tried new things. Honestly, I don't think this game deserved the amount of hate it got. When I play a RE game, I want to save the world from zombies as one of my favorite STARS members, or their family members and best friends, get scared or at least very concerned, and have fun. For me, this game checks off all the necessary boxes.

[h1] Resident Evil 6: Better Than You Remember, Even Better If You Havent Played It. [/h1]

As a longtime Resident Evil fan, there's been one game in the series I've avoided for almost a decade: Resident Evil 6. Back when it was released, it garnered mixed reviews from both fans and critics. It was a dramatic shift from the series' survival horror roots, with multiple campaigns that often felt uneven, a co-op system that made solo play feel like an afterthought, and the abandonment of classic features like a merchant or inventory management. But this Halloween, I decided to finally give it a shot.

From the start, Resident Evil 6 doesn't inspire much confidence. Its sparse main menu feels like something out of an early 2000s multiplayer game. You soon realize that the only way to pause the game is by playing in offline mode, making you feel quite alone, despite having an AI partner always ready to revive you.

The fear factor takes a hit when the game encourages you to holster your gun and engage in frenetic Street Fighter-style melee attacks on the undead. Melee becomes your go-to strategy against hordes of enemies, further diminishing the horror elements.

Resident Evil 6 abandons the survival horror genre. It dabbles in creepiness during Leon's campaign, but the scares are largely absent. The new J'avo enemies, for instance, feel more like regular gun-toting foes with a zombie twist. While the game features some horror-themed missions in catacombs, sewers, and labs, it's primarily an action shooter with grotesque monsters. This departure from the series' roots is likely why Capcom veered back to pure horror with Resident Evil 7.

Looking back now, after Resident Evil's return to survival horror with Resident Evil 7 and Resident Evil Village, it's easier to appreciate Resident Evil 6 for what it truly is: a highly enjoyable action game. The enemy designs are inventive and challenging, and the game sometimes borrows a page from Dead Space by making headshots counterproductive, occasionally causing standard enemies to transform into far more powerful creatures. While it might lack survival horror, it retains Resident Evil's trademark outlandish puzzles.

The game's diverse encounters and settings are perhaps the most exciting in the series, ranging from rooftop chases through apocalyptic cityscapes to Ada Wong's dramatic escape from a sinking submarine. There's even a thrilling sequence where you sink an aircraft carrier using a fighter jet. While the four campaigns occasionally intersect, they mainly tell separate stories in vastly different locations. Admittedly, the narrative is a bit of a mess. I'm not invested in whatchamacallit's sister who's a plant or Ada Wong's murderous clone. It's unfocused, and the broader story strokes are forgettable, but there are enough memorable set pieces and wacky moments to keep you entertained.

So, is it worth revisiting Resident Evil 6 in the wake of Resident Evil Village or checking it out if you've never played it? Absolutely, but think of it as an action game. While it might not live up to its predecessors in terms of its original format, it's a fun Resident Evil game in its own right. The cinematic presentation, filled with action movie clichés, over-the-top dialogue, and tense Quick Time Events, creates an engaging experience during the campaign. However, it might not leave a lasting impression after the credits roll.

Resident Evil 6 is not a perfect game, but it's an enjoyable one, especially if you're looking for action-packed zombie mayhem. It may have divided fans, but it's worth giving it a try for its own unique take on the series.

Badly organized pro tips for having fun:

- Get in melee and use melee attacks. Shoot enemies in the head or knee to open up unique attacks; almost every enemy in the game has a melee prompt from multiple angles. Some bosses do too.
- Roll backwards, forwards, roll around on the ground. Roll sideways up the stairs and through vents. Aim + A button (X on PS controller) to roll around, keep holding aim to stay prone. Tap sideways to roll around.
- Hold B (or Circle on PS controller) and yell at your friends. Yell "NO" when they tell you to open a door. If you're at the door, spam the button until you start yelling.
- Left Trigger + Right Trigger together do a "quick shot" which takes pressure off and opens up enemies for melee follow ups. You get different animations for these ones VS the headshot stagger prompts. Also good for hitting small critters it's hard to aim at. Use these moves, explore your options.
- The healing item refills your stamina (see: melee meter). Using them next to a friend (both sprays and tictacs) heals you both for an empty square of health, plus whatever is currently partly-empty.
- Many attacks can be "parried" with the right timing of a melee prompt. More unique counters, animations, fun.
- I like all the campaigns, but I think the order from best to worst is Leon > Jake > Chris. I'd play Leon > Chris > Jake for a first go through.
- The inventory system sucks and gets worse when you have a full arsenal. Throw away ammo/grenades you don't like if you want room for other stuff, you'll replace it later. You can overflow your healing container up to 17 held at once (then it cannot hold more until you are at 11 charges or less).

[b]Yo, fellow survivors! Strap in and get ready for a wild ride through the apocalypse with Resident Evil 6, a game that's as action-packed as it is cheesy. Let's break it down and see if this zombie-slaying extravaganza is worth your time.

First things first, let's talk about the gameplay. It's like a buffet of destruction, with three different campaigns to sink your teeth into. Whether you're blasting zombies as Leon Kennedy, kicking ass as Chris Redfield, or doing ninja moves as Ada Wong, there's something here for everyone. And let me tell ya, the action is as fast and furious as Vin Diesel on a caffeine bender.

But it ain't all sunshine and rainbows, my dudes. Resident Evil 6 is about as over-the-top as a Hollywood blockbuster, with more explosions than a Michael Bay movie and more melodrama than a soap opera. And let me tell ya, the story is about as coherent as my grandma after one too many glasses of wine. But hey, when you're mowing down zombies with a rocket launcher, who cares about plot holes, am I right?

Now, let's talk about the graphics. They're like a double-edged sword, my dudes. On one hand, you got some pretty sweet visuals that'll make you feel like you're right in the middle of a zombie apocalypse. On the other hand, you got some wonky animations and character models that'll make you wonder if the developers ran out of budget halfway through.

But the real star of the show is the co-op. Whether you're teaming up with your buddies online or going old-school with split-screen, there's nothing quite like taking down hordes of zombies with your best buds by your side. And let me tell ya, the camaraderie that comes from surviving the apocalypse together is something special.

Now, I gotta keep it real with you, Resident Evil 6 ain't perfect. The controls can be about as clunky as a three-legged horse, and the QTEs will make you wanna throw your controller out the window. But hey, when you're knee-deep in zombie guts and saving the world from certain doom, those issues seem minor in comparison.

So, if you're looking for a game that's equal parts cheesy action and zombie-slaying goodness, then Resident Evil 6 is the game for you. Grab your weapons, grab your buddies, and get ready for a wild ride through the apocalypse. Just don't forget to bring plenty of snacks and ammo, 'cause you're gonna need 'em both.[/b]

I'm not an RE purist or anything, but this game is such a mixed bag.
Aside from the great visuals (and incredible performance on Steam Deck), it really doesn't have much going for it.
The game seems to want to indulge old fans with returning characters and nods to moments from past games, while simultaneously abandoning everything that made those games great.
The classic horror elements from RE 0-3 are completely absent here. Make no mistake, this is not a horror game; this is an action game.
The over-the-shoulder camera from RE 4/5 are here, but it just doesn't work like it should. The game is constantly trying to pull your attention in multiple directions at once, and it makes for an often frustrating experience.
The inventory management is worse than ever. I don't expect a full attache case like we had in RE 4 (the game is too fast-paced to make that work), but you're constantly given way more ammo than you could possibly need, and I often found myself just leaving things behind because I had no more room to carry anything.
The story is all over the place, made worse by the fact that you'll need to play through 4 separate campaigns to get the full picture. These campaigns are filled with the most inane dialogue, campy character moments, and baffling design choices I've ever seen in an RE game.
Worst of all, and by a large margin, is that the game seems to have no interest in letting you actually play it. Most of the actual interesting set pieces are just cutscenes with a heap of QTEs. If you absolutely must play this one, you'll want to play co-op, because otherwise you'll just be standing around waiting for your AI teammate to run around in some unseen hallways until they hit some unseen switch. 
If you play solo, be sure to go in with tempered expectations. If you're looking to experience more classic RE goodness, this isn't it. You're going to be getting a generic zombie shooter that wants to be John Woo's Stranglehold, and it unfortunately falls flat on its face time and time again.

[b][h2]Pros:[/h2][/b]
✅ [b]Combat system.[/b] The gunplay and melee system are fast, fluid, and flexible. You can move more while aiming, walking, running, shooting, diving, hiding behind cover, or shooting while lying completely prone. There's also a dedicated stamina bar for melee, letting you chain into cinematic finishers. Depending on the situation, you can knock enemies down, kick them away, follow up on a stunned enemy, or use the environment to perform contextual attacks. You can also parry right before an enemy strikes and chain [i]those[/i] attacks. The wide variety of guns and melee moves gives you plenty of options for dealing with enemies, and the weapons themselves feel weighty and satisfying to fire.

✅ [b]Co-op system.[/b] If there's one thing that makes RE6 significantly more enjoyable, it's playing with another person. You can revive each other, coordinate during fights, split up to handle different enemies, and help each other through some of the game's more frustrating sections. Honestly, I probably would have had a much worse time playing this solo. I had no issues with joining my friend, either.

[b][h2]Cons:[/h2][/b]
🟥 [b]Everything else.[/b] Oh, boy, where to start? The [b]writing, first, is dogwater.[/b] The less said, the better. Actually, wait, no, I can't let sleeping dogs lie; I gotta get my thoughts out. Look, the RE series isn't known for its literary merit, but at least it was fine, if not cheesy. But with RE6, the story is ridiculous, over-the-top, and nonsensical, and it's filled to the brim with Hollywood-esque action cutscenes and explosions. So many explosions. The "four campaigns" did naught for the story and characters except muddle the player's understanding of the timeline and plot. The characters are just as bland as the story. Piers and Jake are the most mid men in existence, and even returning characters like Leon or Chris feel dumbed down to fit the plot. 

🟥 [b] The boss battles are padded bullet sponges.[/b] They literally fit the definition of the word. One chapter in Leon's campaign was an hour-long boss fight. These encounters lack enough variety to justify how often the boss advances to its next stage.

🟥 [b]The phone menu system and inventory management in this game are abysmal and convoluted.[/b] Instead of having a simple, intuitive inventory (like a briefcase...) where I can quickly see what I have and move things around, I'm constantly navigating through menus and trying to figure out what the game actually wants me to press. Managing weapons, ammo, healing items, and other gear feels unnecessarily cumbersome, especially when I'm in an action-heavy section and just want to switch something or use an item. The phone menu is somehow even worse. Why is this a phone? Why am I navigating important game settings through a stupid little phone interface? And, most importantly, why doesn't opening this thing just pause the damn game? If I'm trying to change a setting or figure out what I'm doing, I don't want enemies attacking me while I'm buried in a menu. It's one of those design decisions that feels like it exists because someone thought it looked cool rather than because it actually makes the game better.

🟥 [b]Wonky camera angles.[/b] I actually got [i]nauseous[/i] from RE6's jerky camera work because the camera is always fighting you. It constantly interrupts the action to draw your attention to the thousandth building on fire while you slowly amble along while things are trying to kill you. Let me play the fucking game. I don't need another cinematic camera angle showing me something exploding when I'm already in the middle of a fight.

🟥 [b]Incredibly annoying and present QTEs.[/b] They add nothing and can instantly kill you when you're not expecting it.

🟥 [b]Cringe fan service.[/b] Listen, it gets to a point where I'm side-eyeing you for jerking off to some pixels. Because, man, this game is so horny it feels like watching a movie with your mom and suddenly realizing, “Oh god. We both have to sit through this.” Sure, Ada gets copious ass shots while crawling through vents. Whatever. But for Sherry? Ass shots, jiggle physics, and a revealing hospital gown when you're introduced as a kid? (Like, you can't possibly tell me these women are doing blackflips and kung fu without bras.) And don't even get me started on whatever the fuck Deborah's (bad) boss fight is. It is an incredibly strange tonal choice to watch Helena grieve over her sister while the game frames the monster as sexual spectacle, writhing around naked and moaning. I found it more uncomfortable than entertaining, and I genuinely have no idea what the writers were going for.

It's funny, because on my first playthrough I hated Resident Evil 6 so much I uninstalled it and I wasn't even half way through Leon Chapter 1. After sitting down and be patient enough to finish all the campaigns, my opinions changed: It's a damn fine co-op action game. I went in expecting a Resident Evil game which I shouldn't have, that was probably why I despised it a lot in the first place.

[u][b]Things that Resident Evil 6 did well[/b][/u]

• [b]Well paced for an action game.[/b] After fights you get room to breathe before facing other waves of enemies.
• [b]The story is decent.[/b] This may be controversial but I quite enjoyed the story despise the criticism it has. It might not be as good as other Resident Evil games but still pretty fun on its own.
• [b]The characters.[/b] After finishing the game I appreciate so much more of Leon, Chris and Ada. The new characters such as Jake and grown-up Sherry are pretty interesting as well (except for Helena, she's kinda meh but I don't hate her). I feel like they've done a really good job writing them in this game.
• [b]You can finally run![/b] No more of that Resident Evil 4 and 5 trotting.
• [b]Level design is pretty well done for an action game.[/b] It's easy to follow and there are extra stuffs to find along the way as well.
• [b]The game's length.[/b] Resident Evil 6 is the longest game of the franchise, so if you enjoy games that run for more than 20 hours, this is for you.
• [b]Co-op is fun with friends.[/b] Remember to bring some friends with you, because randoms might try to friendly fire you (this happened to me, yup).

[u][b]Things that Resident Evil 6 did not so well[/b][/u]

• [b]Inventory management.[/b] This is the biggest con of Resident Evil 6 for me. Inventory feels clunky, you can basically see it as non-existent. It's just downright horrendous, even Resident Evil 5 did a better job with this.
• [b]Identity.[/b] The developers tried so hard to please every fans that they ended up disappointing everyone. It clearly does not feel like a Resident Evil game, and the horror that I loved in the older titles was never found in this title.
• [b]The atrocity of quick time events made its return![/b] They really prove time and time again that QTEs are really the worst thing that ever happened to this franchise. Thankfully this game has more tolerable QTEs than RE4 or RE5 but everytime you come across one you just wanna rip your head out.
• [b]Sudden camera angle changes in some segments.[/b] You cannot believe how many times I have died because this game decides to bring back fixed camera angle during tense moments?? It's a really annoying and pesky feature, and it's frequent enough to drive you mad.

[u][b]Every Resident Evil 6's campaign[/b][/u]

You can skip this part if you don't want any spoilers.

• [b]Leon's campaign[/b] is targeted to the zombie fans and the likes. This is supposed to please the Resident Evil fans who love the older titles but it was done rather... poorly. Zombies can use weapons and it looks goofy as hell. Generally, this campaign is okay and the final chapter is kinda epic. 
• [b]Chris' campaign[/b] is for Resident Evil 5 lovers. They feature the same-ish enemies from RE5 (called the J'avo). The combat/melee attacks feel really satisfying with Chris (don't know if it's the same for Piers but it probably is). Overall, I like the story side better than the gameplay side, but it's a decent campaign.
• [b]Jake's campaign[/b] is kinda a mix of Leon and Chris? It's hard to explain, but apparently Jake can do really good melee attacks (I didn't know, I was playing as Sherry). But otherwise, the story and the gameplay is fine on this one.
• [b]Ada's campaign[/b] is for the puzzle suckers from the older RE games. Features plenty of puzzle, and you get the choice of doing the campaign alone or multiplayer which is pretty cool. Ada's coolness is on point, the gameplay and plot is pretty a-okay as well.

Resident Evil 6 is an enormous, action-driven interpretation of the survival horror series that trades much of the franchise’s slower tension for cinematic spectacle, fast combat, and cooperative chaos. Developed and published by Capcom, it brings together several established characters while introducing new faces in a story built around a rapidly escalating global bioterrorism crisis. Rather than following one protagonist through a single adventure, the game divides its narrative across interconnected campaigns, creating one of the largest and most varied single-player and cooperative experiences in the series.

The central threat is the C-virus, a biological weapon capable of producing zombies and increasingly bizarre mutations. Leon S. Kennedy, Chris Redfield, Jake Muller, Sherry Birkin, Ada Wong, and other characters become involved from different perspectives. Their journeys occasionally intersect, allowing events witnessed in one campaign to gain additional meaning when experienced from another. This approach gives the story considerable scale, although its constant escalation can make the narrative feel more like an international disaster movie than a tightly controlled horror story.

Each campaign adopts a somewhat different style. Leon’s chapters contain many of the strongest horror influences, particularly when zombies, dark environments, and confined locations dominate the opening portions. Chris receives a more military-focused storyline built around firefights, squad operations, and overwhelming enemy forces. Jake’s campaign combines gunplay with powerful melee abilities, chase sequences, and repeated confrontations with dangerous creatures. Ada’s scenario adds another layer to the mystery and helps connect important pieces of the overall narrative. This variety keeps the campaigns distinct, but the transitions between horror, military action, melodrama, and blockbuster spectacle can create noticeable tonal inconsistency.

Combat represents one of the game’s most significant departures from older entries. Characters are considerably more mobile and can shoot while moving, dodge attacks, roll across the ground, slide, take cover, and perform numerous close-range attacks. The melee system is particularly enjoyable once its possibilities become familiar. Firearms remain essential, but combining gunfire with physical attacks can conserve ammunition while making encounters more dynamic. The mechanics have more depth than the game initially communicates, and learning how to use movement effectively can dramatically improve the experience.

Enemies complement this aggressive combat design. Familiar zombies appear alongside the J’avo, intelligent infected opponents capable of using weapons and undergoing dramatic mutations after suffering injuries. These transformations can alter limbs, produce defensive structures, or turn previously ordinary opponents into much more dangerous creatures. Larger biological monstrosities and elaborate bosses frequently appear as well. Creature design embraces grotesque body horror, although the sheer number of massive encounters eventually reduces some of their shock value.

Cooperative play is one of the strongest reasons to experience the game. Most campaigns pair two characters together, making teamwork feel like a natural part of progression rather than an optional addition. Playing alongside another person makes firefights, boss encounters, and hectic set pieces considerably more entertaining. Solo players can rely on an AI partner, which generally keeps the campaign functional but cannot replicate the coordination or unpredictability of a human teammate. Certain crossover moments also allow characters from separate storylines to participate in the same encounter, reinforcing the interconnected nature of the overall adventure.

Character progression revolves around collecting skill points and purchasing abilities. These skills can improve weapon performance, defensive capabilities, melee effectiveness, and other useful attributes. The system provides flexibility and rewards continued play, although players expecting extensive weapon customization or traditional resource-management mechanics may find it comparatively straightforward. Inventory management has also been streamlined to accommodate the faster pace.

The biggest weakness is the relentless dependence on spectacle. Explosions, vehicle sections, collapsing environments, chase sequences, quick-time events, scripted escapes, and gigantic bosses arrive with remarkable frequency. Individual sequences can be exciting, but the constant escalation leaves little room for suspense to develop naturally. Camera behavior can occasionally become troublesome during frantic encounters, while certain scripted sequences demand immediate reactions without providing much opportunity to understand the danger. These design choices are likely to frustrate players hoping for the deliberate pacing associated with classic survival horror.

There is substantial content beyond the story campaigns. Mercenaries is particularly well suited to the expanded combat mechanics, challenging players to defeat enemies rapidly while maintaining combos and pursuing increasingly high scores. The PC edition also offers The Mercenaries No Mercy, where larger enemy groups create intense battles designed around mastering movement, weapons, and melee techniques. Agent Hunt provides a different concept by allowing players to control infected creatures and interfere with another player’s campaign. These additional modes give the combat system room to shine without the narrative interruptions found throughout the main story.

Visually, the game still delivers an effective mixture of detailed characters, grotesque monsters, atmospheric environments, and elaborate cinematic sequences. Locations change frequently, helping the lengthy campaigns maintain visual variety. Sound effects give weapons and creatures appropriate impact, while the dramatic soundtrack reinforces the blockbuster tone. It may not consistently produce fear, but it remains capable of creating impressive action sequences and memorable biological horrors.

Steam Deck compatibility is a notable advantage for portable players. Resident Evil 6 is Steam Deck Verified, meaning it is officially considered suitable for Valve’s handheld environment. Controller functionality fits the game naturally, interface elements remain practical for portable use, and the experience can be played without requiring extensive configuration. Its mission-based structure also translates conveniently to handheld sessions.

Resident Evil 6 is best approached as a cooperative action game infused with Resident Evil characters, creatures, and bioterrorism rather than as a traditional survival horror experience. Its excessive spectacle and uneven tone prevent it from achieving the focused tension of the franchise’s strongest horror installments, but its responsive combat, multiple campaigns, diverse playable characters, cooperative systems, mutation mechanics, and substantial bonus content provide considerable entertainment. For players comfortable with its unapologetically action-heavy direction, there is a surprisingly deep and content-rich adventure beneath the explosions.

I'll try to keep this as short as possible.
Resident Evil 6 is not what an oldschool/hardcore gamer would call a "RE game". It's an attempt to make the game more over the top, action-y and cinematic as much as possible while having that cheesy dialogue and plenty of references to older titles. Hence it's an action game with barely any horror. If you're able to accept that then you'll also be able to enjoy it. The game has 4 co-op campaigns that have 5 chapters each (average chapter length is 1 hour), 2 characters you can play as in each campaign and 5 difficulty settings. Considering it's a co-op game you should probably play and laugh with your friends, but in worst case scenario you can also play with the AI. Unlike RE5's Sheva your AI partner is completely self-sustaining and you don't have to babysit. The mechanics here are the most advanced in the series and a lot of people enjoy Mercenaries mode because of it. Now that I've mentioned the campaigns - we can say that to complete the on 1 difficulty with both characters already will take quite a while, now let's multiply this by 5 difficulty settings and we hell of a lot gameplay time. The game has huge replay value (far bigger than RE2 or REmake) and with a right friend you'll be able to enjoy this for quite a while. If you want more then there are competitive DLC modes. If you're looking for people to play with then you should check http://steamcommunity.com/groups/re6mp

AMD users should be aware that latest drivers result in the infamous black screen on startup. If you wait for a couple of minutes the game will load. The time depends on how juicy your system is.

Again, If you're going to play this game because it's a RE title then you'll have a bad time. If you're in for some laughs and co-op then this is easily the best co-op game of that year.
And if you're looking for actual horror then you should get Resident Evil Remake Remaster and Resident Evil 0 Remaster.

Finally, here's a list of alphabetical pros and cons.
Pros:
-Agent Hunt. A special game mode in which YOU take control of the enemy. You can join any open lobby and try to take down players that are just playing the game. Requires patience, skill and preferably a partner.
-Characters. RE6 offers both Chris and Leon as playable characters in separate campaigns. Not only that, there are total of 8 (campaign) and 13 (no mercy mercenaries) playable characters.
-Collectibles. Just like RE4,5 RE6 has some collectibles that you can find (serpents than unlock documents and figurines).
-Completionist friendly. There's a lot of things you can complete in the game and boy you'll have to spend more than a few hundreds of hours to do that.
-Controls. The controls now are less tanky and more action-y, fluent. You can manually dodge, counter, slide, etc. After playing RE6 for a while and returning to RE5 you'll see what I mean. The only downside is that you have to learn and master the controls yourself (which is not an easy thing to do). Be sure to check Archon's "Basic and Advanced Mechanics" guide.
-DLCs. They offer fun competitive multiplayer minigames and extra achievements for them. These game modes are as fun as Mercenaries. Survivors is a deathmatch mode (standard and team, up to 6 players, most popular). Onslaught is a mix between Dr. Mario and Mercenaries (kill enemies to send them to your opponent, 2 players only). Predator is the mode in which you take control of Ustanak and try to defeat other players (up to 6 players, 2nd most popular). Siege is a BOWs vs humans team match in which you have to try to save an NPC (up to 6 players, least popular).
-Enemies. Quite a huge variety of them this time. Also they can mutate on the go. They act, look differently and have different attacks.
-Events. residentevil.net offers different types of events so you can unlock some in-game on website goodies.
-Melee. You can use knifes and your fists/legs to punch bould... enemies and execute them in most brutal ways. Source of the wrestling simulator game jokes.
-Mercenaries. Many people (sometimes jokingly) say that it's the only reason why you should get this game. Well, they're not far from the truth either. This mode offers a fun solo/duo survival challenge on 10 different maps, provides you with all characters and special costumes for each. There's also a PC exclusive "No Mercy" mode which is a Left 4 Dead crossover (characters and enemies) and it's even more challenging.
-Nemesis v2. The game has an enemy that is similar to Nemesis from RE3.
-Options. The game allows some nice tweaks including camera placement, FOV and crosshair swaps. Be sure to check the options in the main menu (they're more advanced than in-game's).
-Ranking system. You can earn ranks on each chapter for each character. Great thing from completionists. Ranking is based on your accuracy, kills, time and deaths.
-Replay value. The main story offers a lot of content that can be replayed many times.
-Skills. You can earn points and purchase skills that can alter the gameplay a bit.
-Soundtrack. Many people either forget about it or it gets lost as background noise. The game has a great huge soundtrack that adds a lot to the game.
-Statistics. Residentevil.net offers advanced game statistics.
-Story. Many people would say that this is BS, but I think that RE6 offers better, brighter and more silly, over the top story than ever before.
-Unlockable free content. You might say that it's similar to an on-disc DLC, but I don't think it's bad. On residentevil.net you can unlock special files and costumes for your minigames.
-Variety of weapons. Knives, guns, machine guns, assault rifles, sniper rifles, crossbow, grenade launchers, magnums, remote bombs, grenades, etc.

Cons:
-Bugs. The game still has some connectivity issues and sometimes it crashes. Some issues might appear if you have incredibly high ping.
-Camera. Might be one of the reasons why you'll die a bunch of times.
-Controls. Some people may find the controls a bit too difficult/messy. They require a lot of time to master and even an experienced player may not know all the tricks. On top of that, an experienced Agent Hunter can easily take down newbie agents.
-DLCs. They're not free. You have to pay for them. It's hard to find active sessions, but people are playing them.
-Enemies. While there are still "zombie" BOWs now there are also J'avos, that can use weapons, can communicate with each other (similar to plagas infected).
-Graphics. Generally OK, but texture-wise this is a console port and there are plenty of dodgy textures.
-Puzzles. Some of them are ar simple (stupid), just like in oldschool REs. But due to fast paced gameplay you don't stumble upon them as often as you'd like to.
-QTEs. The game has quite a lot of them, but they aren't difficult and not as unforgiving as in RE4/5. QTEs can be turned off completely.
-Single player. Playing alone isn't as fun as it's in co-op. You can't disable your AI partner either.
-Story. You could say that it's too over the top and less realistic than before. Some may say that it's a B-movie, just like RE1.
-Survival horror. Barely any left.

FAQ.
Q: I've launched the game and I'm greeted with a settings screen and then the game starts. Where's the main menu?
A: Upon first launch you're greeted with a 15 minute prologue. It's infested with QTEs that luckily aren't even in the main game.

Q: Can I co-op the prologue?
A: Prologue is actually a modified Leon 5 chapter. So yes, by playing chapter 5.

Finally, I can't keep everything in mind, so remind me about things I forgot about in comments.
Final verdict: Would I recommend this as a RE game? No. Would I recommend this as a game? Hell yes. If you like the combat and the challenge - it's simply enjoyable.
